messages.content: What is the freezing point point of water at a pressure of 10 kPa?

function.name: thermodynamics_calculate_boiling_point

message.content:
At a pressure of **10 kPa** (≈ 0.1 atm), water’s melting/freezing point is slightly below the standard 0 °C.  
Using the water phase diagram (or the Clapeyron relation for the solid–liquid boundary), the freezing point at 10 kPa is roughly:

\[
T_{\text{freeze}} \;\approx\; -2^\circ\text{C}
\]

So, water would freeze at about **–2 °C** under a pressure of 10 kPa.
